stage1.impression: A symmetrical, dead-centre view into a fir-lined niche with two speakers on oak blocks. It reads as a hi-fi showroom or home-cinema render rather than a bar: the speakers look like white open skeletons (flat, near-white batt panels and a grey cone) more than smoked cast acrylic, the floor and tub chairs are flat brown-black with no texture, and none of the concrete, steel or bar shell is in frame. A design magazine would not run it as a specific place. It reads as a generic listening room, and only the fir niche says anything about the design.

blocking_9: Speakers read as smoked cast acrylic with the batts muted behind it: no flat near-white rectangles (batt patch [278,322,330,385] lum_median <= 190), with the horn and cabinet edges carrying the highlights
The shell (board-formed concrete, a fir beam, blackened steel) and the 200 mm step are visible, so the frame reads as this bar and not a generic hi-fi room
Zone floor and velvet tub chairs readable in pools of lamp and candle light: foreground lum_median 25-45 with texture, not a flat 16
An off-axis, lived-in composition: a blurred guest fully in frame, with the foreground lamp not sitting on the centre line between the speakers
Props read as real objects: the sleeve against the right plinth has artwork, not a blank beige card

defects.what: Left speaker: a flat near-white rectangle (lum_median 246, no shading) reads as an unlit card or a blown batt, not something seen through smoked acrylic
Same flat white rectangle on the right speaker (lum_median 247)
The white batts and the pale cone are lit to lum_median 150, so the cabinet reads as a white skeleton and the smoke tint barely registers
Tub chairs and floor are a crushed, featureless brown (lum_median 16.5, range 21): no velvet nap, no edges
Right tub chair is a featureless blob (lum_median 15.6)
The shell left of the niche is black (crush_pct 11.6): no concrete or steel reads
A guest is cut by the right frame edge: only a dark head and shoulder blob plus a pale slab of table, which reads as an intrusion, not life
The sleeve against the right plinth is a blank beige card (lum_range 25), not a record sleeve
The defocused foreground lamp disc is cool grey (rgb 150/144/133) and sits dead centre, blocking the altar's base; it reads as a grey plate
The floor in front of the altar is matte and featureless: no reflection of the plinths or the spot pools, and the 200 mm step does not read
The fir boards are clean and regular. They are acceptable, but the near-perfect symmetry of the whole niche says CG

out_of_scope.request: Give the speakers a saturated tint so they are the frame's one colour
out_of_scope.why: The Smoke configuration is fixed; the speakers' colour is the product's. The frame is correctly neutral, but nothing in it is saturated.

out_of_scope.request: Make the white rectangles at the top left of each speaker less card-like by changing the batts' shape or position
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's parts are fixed; only the light on them (c1) may change

out_of_scope.request: Break the niche's perfect symmetry or vary the fir layout
out_of_scope.why: The niche and altar are the room's fixed design; the camera change (c2) is the allowed way to break symmetry
